problem: A point $P$ has Cartesian coordinates $(-8,-15).$ What are the polar coordinates of $P?$ Round your answer to two decimal places where necessary.
worked_solution:
First, we determine $r:$

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{(-8)^{2}+(-15)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{64+225} \\  & =\sqrt{289} \\  & =17\end{aligned}
$$

For the reference angle, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\theta }_{R} & =|\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{y}{x})| \\  & =|\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{-15}{-8})| \\  & ≈1.080\,84.\end{aligned}
$$

Since the point $P$ lies in the third quadrant, we add the reference angle to $\pi ,$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\theta  & =\pi +{\theta }_{R} \\  & =\pi +1.080\,84 \\  & ≈4.22,\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to two decimal places. Therefore, the polar coordinates of $P$ are  $(17,4.22).$
